transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get this pre-air lock meeting started. We've got the finale going live Saturday at 9 PM Eastern, and we need to finalize the voting package today so standards, platform production, rights, and data protection can all document it before transmission. The current draft has SMS and online portal voting open to our broadcast audience. Before I make the binding call on the final package, I want to hear from each of you — are there any issues, concerns, or things I should know about from your areas?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something from the standards side. After the draft voting rules were circulated, I issued the network's current standards memo, which sets binding requirements: voters must be at least 13 years old, each voter may cast exactly one vote per verified account, and voting must close at 9:50 PM Eastern. The current draft package doesn't yet reflect these requirements, so we need to make sure the final package incorporates all three before transmission.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue from platform production. I completed the platform certification test this morning, and the SMS integration failed certification — only the web portal passed. So as it stands, SMS voting is not certified for use on Saturday. Additionally, the approved web portal requires account verification before a vote is accepted, which aligns with Julian's standards memo on verified accounts but means we need to drop SMS from the final package.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a rights issue. I obtained the finalist label's written approval today, and it confirms that the voting interface may display finalist names and approved headshots, but it may NOT use any finalist performance audio or video. The current draft interface still contains performance clips, so those must be removed before transmission or we'll be in breach of the label's approval.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to flag a data protection issue. My privacy review with the voting vendor, completed this week, limits participation to viewers physically located in the United States and Canada, and requires voter identifiers to be deleted within 30 days. The current draft still describes worldwide participation and has no deletion step, so both of these need to be corrected in the final package before transmission.
transcript.speaker: A5
